Anthony Hudson

Libertarian candidate for Governor / Lt. Governor, Michigan · Open seat

Truck driver and small business owner (Grand Blanc Township, Genesee County)

Anthony Hudson is a truck driver and small business owner from Grand Blanc Township. He ran in the 2024 Republican primary for a U.S. House seat, entered the 2026 governor's race as a Republican, and switched to the Libertarian Party in February 2026. The Libertarian Party nominated him for governor on June 28, 2026, with Beau Parmenter as his running mate, and he is on the November 3 ballot as the Libertarian nominee, although the state party disavowed his campaign in late September 2026.

Where Hudson stands

Taxes and school choice
His campaign website lists getting rid of property taxes and the state income tax as a priority.
Size and accountability of government
Proposes making the Michigan Legislature part-time with part-time pay. Says Lansing politicians have expanded government while taxpayers face rising costs and excessive regulations.
Data centers
Wants lawmakers to write rules for data centers, fine violators $1 million a day, and send that money to affected communities. Took part in an October 2026 Capitol protest against hyperscale data centers.
Renewable energy / EVs
Would repeal Public Act 233 of 2023, which gave the Public Service Commission siting authority over large renewable energy projects, and return that control to local governments. His website calls for removing solar and wind farms from state land.
Auto insurance
Proposes moving Michigan from no-fault to at-fault auto insurance.
Constitutional freedoms
Says he is running to protect constitutional freedoms. Argues that the comments that led the Libertarian Party to disavow him were protected by his First Amendment right to free speech.

Background

  • Truck driver for about 20 years; small business owner in Grand Blanc Township
  • Moved to Michigan in 2012
  • Ran in the 2024 Republican primary for U.S. House; lost to Paul Junge
  • Started a campaign for the 2026 Republican nomination for governor in March 2025
  • Switched to the Libertarian Party in February 2026
  • Nominated as the Libertarian candidate for governor on June 28, 2026, with Beau Parmenter for lieutenant governor
  • Libertarian Party of Michigan censured him in September 2026 and disavowed his campaign on Sept. 27–28, 2026; he is still the Libertarian nominee on the ballot
